- For product deactivation models (M12, M17), the presence of 0.5 P at t=0 will cause immediate catalyst deactivation. We will observe a significantly depressed initial rate and an early plateau (incomplete conversion) compared to models without P-dependence.
- For substrate deactivation (M16), the high initial [S] will drive rapid irreversible formation of inactive_catS2. The reaction will stall early due to catalyst depletion, but the initial rate won't be suppressed by P.
- For the substrate-activated model (M7, where S + catS <=> catS2 -> P + catS), the high [S] will strongly accelerate the reaction because the productive intermediate requires two substrate molecules. It will not stall prematurely.
- For standard models (M1, M2), the reaction will follow typical saturation kinetics and proceed to full conversion, with the initial rate largely unaffected by the initial P (unless strongly reversible, but it won't permanently stall).
This single experiment simultaneously probes product inhibition, substrate inhibition, and higher-order substrate dependence.
</hypothesis>
